parsed.why: Courts repeatedly enjoin the state's own anti-trans laws (markers, bathrooms, care) — the sole division improving in 2026. No facilities ban in force, no violence recorded, but hostile statutes persist atop a restrictive national regime.

Bathroom-bounty law covering airports and government buildings, criminal and civil penalties with private suits, invalidated IDs; flagged Do Not Travel. Tier-1 universal exposure layered on a hostile national border and custody regime.

Among Most Protective: gender-identity nondiscrimination since 2001, hate-crime enhancements, panic defence repealed 2018, X markers, shield laws; no facilities ban or violence recorded, but the national border and facilities layer still applies.

Low-Risk tier: codified gender-identity nondiscrimination, explicit hate-crime coverage and panic-defence abolition, conversion-therapy ban, declaration-based ID change; no facilities ban or violence data, though the national regime and unrepealed sodomy statute remain.

Most-protective group with shield laws and comprehensive insurance, but prisons punished a trans woman by returning her to birth-sex housing — documented state custody exposure; two pending ballot initiatives; national regime unchanged.
